units.source_text: 薰中纳言思量：“大女公子前因丧服在身，所以未便答应我的要求，如今丧服即将脱去了。”

en.t: Kaoru, the Middle Counselor, thought, "The elder lady could not readily answer my request before because she was still in mourning, but now she is about to put off her mourning clothes."

units.source_text: 他焦灼地等到了九月里，又到宇治来访问。

en.t: He waited impatiently until the ninth month, then came again to Uji to visit.

units.source_text: 他要求同上次一样直接晤谈。

en.t: He asked, as he had before, to speak with her directly.

units.source_text: 侍女们向大女公子传达，大女公子说：“我心绪不佳，身体很不舒服……”

en.t: The gentlewomen conveyed this to the elder lady, but she said, "My spirits are poor, and I feel very unwell..."

units.source_text: 说了种种理由，不肯和他会面。

en.t: She gave various reasons and refused to meet him.

units.source_text: 薰君说：“如此无情，真是意想不到的啊！

en.t: Lord Kaoru said, "I never imagined she could be so heartless!

units.source_text: 不知旁人看了作何感想。”

en.t: I wonder what others would think if they saw this."

units.source_text: 便写了一封信叫人送进去。

en.t: He then wrote a letter and had someone carry it inside.

units.source_text: 大女公子复道：“如今虽过周忌，脱去丧服，但悲哀反而加深，心绪郁结，不能应对。”

en.t: The elder lady replied, "Although the first anniversary has now passed and I have taken off my mourning clothes, my grief has only deepened, and my heart is too oppressed to receive anyone."

units.source_text: 薰君未便再说怨恨的话，便召唤那老侍女弁君来前，和她谈了许多话。

en.t: Lord Kaoru could not very well complain further, so he called the old gentlewoman Ben no Kimi before him and spoke with her at length.

units.source_text: 这里的侍女们度着世无其例的孤寂生涯，其惟一的慰藉者只是薰中纳言一人。

en.t: The gentlewomen here lived a life of loneliness almost without parallel, and their only comfort was Kaoru, the Middle Counselor.

units.source_text: 她们都在谈论：“若能如我们所愿，小姐配了这个郎君，移居常人所住的京都，那才是幸福了。”

en.t: They all said to one another, "If only things went as we wished, and our lady were matched with this gentleman and moved to the capital where ordinary people live, that would be true happiness."

units.source_text: 大家相与商量，只想把薰君带进大女公子房中去。

en.t: They discussed it together, thinking only of how to bring Lord Kaoru into the elder lady's room.

units.source_text: 大女公子并不深悉此种情况，但她想道：“那人如此特别亲近这老侍女，可知这老侍女同情于他，或许怀着不良之心。

en.t: The elder lady did not know the full situation, but she thought, "Since he is so especially close to this old gentlewoman, she must sympathize with him and may even be harboring improper intentions.

units.source_text: 试看古代小说中所述，女子为非作歹，往往非出自心所愿，大都是由侍女诱导的。

en.t: As the old tales show, when women go astray, it is often not from their own desire but because they are led on by their gentlewomen.

units.source_text: 不可不严防的，正是人心。”

en.t: What must be most strictly guarded against is the human heart."

units.source_text: 又想：“如果那人用心深挚，就把妹妹嫁给他吧。

en.t: She also thought, "If his feelings are truly deep and sincere, I should give my younger sister to him.

units.source_text: 照他的性情看来，即使女子相貌不甚美好，一经相逢，决不会冷遇她。

en.t: Judging from his nature, even if a woman were not especially beautiful, once he had met her he would never treat her coldly.

units.source_text: 何况妹妹的相貌，约略窥见便可令人满意。

en.t: All the more so with my sister, whose appearance is enough to satisfy anyone even from a brief glimpse.

units.source_text: 他大约心中满意而口上不说，因为不好意思表示他早就看中妹妹。

en.t: He is probably pleased in his heart but does not say so, because he is embarrassed to show that he noticed my sister long ago.

units.source_text: 他以前说本意不在妹妹而不接受我的劝告，一半是为了不欲使人知道他对我爱情浅薄，有所顾忌而已。”

en.t: When he said before that my sister was not his true intention and refused my advice, it was partly because he feared people would learn how shallow his love for me was."

units.source_text: 但她认为若不预先告知二女公子而独断独行，是罪过的行为。

en.t: But she felt it would be wrong, even sinful, to act on her own without first telling the second lady.

units.source_text: 她推己及人，觉得对她不起，便在对她做了种种闲谈之后开口说：“父亲的遗志，是指望我们即使在世间孤苦度日，也不可轻率嫁人，以致惹人笑话。

en.t: Putting herself in her sister's place, she felt she would be doing her wrong, and after chatting with her about many things, she began, "Father's dying wish was that even if we lived lonely lives in this world, we should not marry rashly and become objects of ridicule.

units.source_text: 父亲在世之时，我们做了他出家的羁绊，扰乱了他的静修，罪业实甚深重。

en.t: While Father was alive, we bound him to the world when he wished to become a monk and disturbed his quiet practice, so our sin is very grave.

units.source_text: 临终时的一句遗言，至少不可违背。

en.t: At the very least, we must not go against the single instruction he left us at his death.

units.source_text: 为此我们孤居独处，并不深感痛苦。

en.t: For that reason, living alone in seclusion does not feel deeply painful to us.

units.source_text: 然而这些侍女常常抱怨我们，认为过分顽强，实在讨厌得很。

en.t: Yet these gentlewomen constantly complain that we are far too stubborn, and it is truly tiresome.

units.source_text: 惟关于你的身世，确是可虑：若与我一样孤居独处，任逝水流年悠悠空过，实甚可怜、可惜而又可悲。

en.t: Only your future truly worries me: if you live alone as I do and let the flowing years pass emptily by, it would be pitiful, regrettable, and sad.

units.source_text: 你总得像世间一般女子那样嫁个夫婿，那么我这个孤独的姐姐也可脸上增光，心情欢慰。”

en.t: You really ought to marry a husband like other women in the world, and then even I, your lonely elder sister, could take pride in it and be comforted."

units.source_text: 二女公子听了心甚不快，怪怨姐姐如何起这念头，便答道：“父亲并非叫姐姐一人独身终老呀！

en.t: The second lady was deeply upset to hear this and resented her sister for thinking such a thing, so she answered, "Father did not tell only you, Sister, to remain unmarried all your life!

units.source_text: 父亲深恐我没有主见，受人欺侮，对我的关念比对姐姐更深呢。

en.t: Father was deeply afraid that I would have no will of my own and be mistreated by others, so his concern for me was even greater than his concern for you.

units.source_text: 为欲慰安姐姐的孤寂，除了由我朝夕奉陪，没有别的办法了。”

en.t: To comfort your loneliness, there is no other way than for me to stay by your side morning and evening."

units.source_text: 她不免对姐姐怨恨。

en.t: She could not help feeling resentful toward her sister.

units.source_text: 姐姐也觉得这话的确对她不起，只得认错：“我无非是为了这些侍女们常常怨我太怪僻，因此心思迷乱了。”

en.t: The elder sister also felt that these words had indeed wronged her, and she could only admit her fault: "It is simply that these gentlewomen are always reproaching me for being too eccentric, and my thoughts became confused."

units.source_text: 便不再谈此事。

en.t: After that, she said no more about the matter.
